name: Shay Boloor
zh_summary: @StockSavvyShay: Ethernet switching is growing 49% a year versus 36% for AI servers as bigger GPU clusters need faster networking, great for $MRVL, $ALAB, $CRDO and $AVGO; $ANET holds ~25% of AI Ethernet switching.
en_summary: @StockSavvyShay: Ethernet switching is growing 49% a year versus 36% for AI servers as bigger GPU clusters need faster networking, great for $MRVL, $ALAB, $CRDO and $AVGO; $ANET holds ~25% of AI Ethernet switching.
text:
One of the most overlooked parts of the AI buildout is that Ethernet switching is growing 49% annually versus 36% for AI servers as larger GPU clusters require increasingly powerful networking.

That’s great for $MRVL, $ALAB, $CRDO and $AVGO because every new generation of AI chips needs faster connections to move data between GPUs, memory and entire server racks.

$ANET is also interesting because it holds ~25% of AI Ethernet switching as hyperscalers are adopting Ethernet to connect massive AI clusters.

The changing demographics and increased population due to the above factors. 

The state responding to protests by increasing social support. 

The continued failure to punish and hold accountable violent and looting rioters. 

Government managed by a massive and growing unelected bureaucracy.

en_summary: CoreWeave $CRWV shares fell 11.9% on Friday to $61.39, extending weekly losses to nearly 25%. Bond yields climbed above 15% and five-year debt insurance hit record highs near 1,195 basis points. The company carries roughly $50-52 billion in debt and lease obligations for AI data-center expansion. Investors are repricing leveraged AI infrastructure as elevated borrowing costs make debt the binding constraint on the AI trade.
text:
CoreWeave $CRWV shares fell -11.9% on Friday to $61.39, extending weekly losses to nearly -25%.

The drop came as yields on some of the company’s bonds climbed above 15% and the cost of insuring its five-year debt hit record highs near 1,195 basis points.

CoreWeave carries roughly $50–52 billion in debt and lease obligations used to fund its AI data-center expansion.

Investors are repricing heavily leveraged AI infrastructure names as borrowing costs remain elevated.

Debt is becoming the binding constraint on the AI trade.

text:
Let’s go back to 2021 when I said no way no how TSLA would deliver anywhere near TSLA management’s  forecast of 20M EVs by 2030 because others would catch up in the EV space to TSLA.   Like now, $TSLA bulls vehemently disagreed saying no one could catch up with TSLA scale and manufacturing expertise. name: The Kobeissi Letter
zh_summary: The number of restaurants in New York dropped about 2,000 YoY in Q1 2026, the largest YoY decline in at least 36 years, surpassing the 2020 pandemic contraction. Eating and drinking places declined YoY for 4 consecutive quarters. Surging costs including insurance, wages, interest rates, utilities and health coverage are crushing New York restaurants.
en_summary: The number of restaurants in New York dropped about 2,000 YoY in Q1 2026, the largest YoY decline in at least 36 years, surpassing the 2020 pandemic contraction. Eating and drinking places declined YoY for 4 consecutive quarters. Surging costs including insurance, wages, interest rates, utilities and health coverage are crushing New York restaurants.
text:
BREAKING: The number of restaurants in New York dropped ~2,000 YoY in Q1 2026, posting its largest YoY decline in at least 36 years.

This surpasses even the worst contraction recorded in any quarter during the 2020 pandemic.

The number of eating and drinking places in New York State has now declined YoY for 4 consecutive quarters, its longest streak since 2021.

This comes as restaurants are facing surging operating expenses, including insurance premiums, wages, interest rates, utilities, and health coverage, with overall costs rising faster than national averages.

Last year, employee health insurance costs jumped +12.9% for New York-area service firms, business insurance rose +7.0%, while utility costs surged +8.5%, according to the Manhattan Chamber of Commerce.

Skyrocketing costs are crushing New York restaurants.

Skyrocketing costs are crushing New York restaurants.
